headline: Arianespace sets a launch window of the twenty-third of November for Ariane 6 flight VA271
summary: Arianespace has announced a launch window on the twenty-third of November for mission VA271, the tenth Ariane 6 flight.
The earlier notice gave thirty-six Amazon Leo satellites and a date of no earlier than that day.
Voyager 1 has become the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth.
In South Korea, KT SAT is to lead a maritime connectivity project with ST Engineering iDirect, and Türkiye's next micro-satellite is due to launch in 2028.
The European Space Agency vote of the tenth of November has no published outcome, and Rome follows on the fifteenth of December.
bottom_line: Ariane 6 flight VA271 now has a stated launch window on the twenty-third of November, and the European Space Agency decisions still run to Rome. The next date that matters is the twenty-third of November.

audio_script:
Good morning. It is Wednesday, the eighteenth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Arianespace has set a launch window for the twenty-third of November. Voyager 1 has become the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth. And Türkiye's next micro-satellite is due to launch in 2028.

Arianespace announced on the eighteenth of November a launch window on the twenty-third of November for mission VA271. It is the tenth Ariane 6 flight. In October, Arianespace had said it would carry thirty-six Amazon Leo satellites, no earlier than that date. The notice now turns the estimate into a window. The launch hour was not given in what we have. The flight follows the Prometheus engine hot-fire of the sixth of November, a step in Europe's work on reusable engines. Separately, Amazon's launch on a Vulcan Centaur failed on the fifteenth of November. Its cause and next flight are still unknown.

Voyager 1 has become the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, after forty-nine years in flight. Signals now take about a day each way, so a reply to any command takes about forty-eight hours. It is a milestone, and it does not change any program pathway.

In Europe, the European Space Agency has not yet signed its contract with MaiaSpace, because of differences over the financing model. The vote of the tenth of November has no published outcome. The launcher financing model is therefore unsettled ahead of the Rome meeting. The next date is Rome, on the fifteenth of December.

In Central and Eastern Europe, the Ukrainian connectivity question stands where it did. President Zelenskyy said on the twelfth of November that speed restrictions on Starlink had been recorded for several days. SpaceX has made no statement. The hope for a Starshield route remains mid-2027. Ukraine's connectivity still rests on Starlink, and no new date is set.

In the Nordics, the Swedish National Space Agency has set its annual event, Rymddagen, for the eighteenth of February 2027. Its November blog marks the Voyager 1 milestone and ESA's Hera asteroid work. It is the next fixed date from the Swedish agency.

In Italy, Iceye has launched a bid of 2.05 billion euros for the launcher maker Avio. The aim is a European space and defence group. It would join a radar satellite maker to a launcher maker. No completion date is given, and we have only a single trade source. In Spain, PLD Space has signed its first commercial launch contract for its Miura 5 rocket. The customer is Mitsubishi Electric. It is the first commercial order for the Spanish rocket, and no launch date is given.

In Eurasia, a joint satellite of the Turkic states is due to launch in 2027. No builder or date is given. It is the one dated Eurasian space item in what we have, and the picture there is thin.

In Türkiye, a new micro-satellite is due to launch in 2028. No month is given. It adds to a national program that also includes a first lunar mission.

In South Korea, KT SAT is to lead a maritime connectivity project with ST Engineering iDirect, of Singapore. It is a national maritime link built on a Singapore supplier. Terms and dates are not given.

In Paraguay, the second national satellite, GuaraníSat-2, has been launched. Japan has agreed a donation of 24 million dollars for satellite technology. Both items extend a small national program with Japanese support. In Mexico, lawmakers approved only 700 million additional pesos for the civil aviation authority in the 2027 budget. The sum is below what the sector sought. This is an aviation item rather than a space one.

In the United States, NASA holds its Artemis dates unchanged after the moon base awards of the ninth of November. Proposals are due on the eighth of December. No fresh source moved the pathway today.

What we are tracking this week is flight VA271 on the twenty-third of November. This month we are tracking whether any outcome of the European Space Agency vote of the tenth of November is published, and whether the Federal Aviation Administration decides on Blue Origin. Its deadline of the thirtieth of October has passed. A January return remains unconfirmed. The heads-up dates are the eighth of December, when Artemis proposals are due, and the fifteenth of December, for Rome. That is the briefing for Wednesday, the eighteenth of November.
